## Format-scoped attributes on Divs

The next block shows the same Div with two format-scoped `style` values.
When rendered to HTML the `html:` prefix wins; when rendered to revealjs the `revealjs:` prefix wins.
The unprefixed `data-note` attribute is preserved in every format.

::: {data-note="kept everywhere" html:style="color: hotpink;" revealjs:style="font-size: 2em;"}
This paragraph is pink in HTML and large in revealjs.
:::

## Override behaviour

A format-scoped attribute appended after a static attribute of the same name overrides it.
In HTML the resolved `style` value is the HTML one.

::: {style="color: gray;" html:style="color: rebeccapurple;"}
This paragraph reads as purple in HTML.
:::

## Format-scoped attributes on Spans

Inline content can carry format-scoped attributes too.
The next sentence styles a [single span]{html:style="background: yellow; padding: 0 0.2em;" pdf:style="\\hl{...}"} only when the active format matches.

## Format-scoped attributes on CodeBlocks

CodeBlocks accept the same syntax.
The HTML output renders this code block with a tinted background.

```{.r html:style="background: #f6f8fa; padding: 0.5em;"}
1 + 1
```

## Unmatched prefixes are dropped

Prefixes that do not resolve to the active format are removed entirely.
The following Div has only `pdf:` and `docx:` attributes; under HTML it renders with no extra attributes.

::: {pdf:style="font-size: 12pt;" docx:custom-style="Note"}
Plain content in HTML; styled in PDF and DOCX.
:::
